claims.explanation: GW-843682X is a PLK1/PLK3 inhibitor, and sensitivity likely reflects dependence on PLK1-driven mitotic progression and/or defective DNA-damage/checkpoint signaling. TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines, suggesting loss of p53-mediated arrest makes cells reliant on PLK1 and vulnerable to its inhibition; co-occurring RAS/RTK pathway activation and SMARCA4 loss may further increase mitotic/transcriptional stress. Resistant lines often retain functional p53-pathway or have mutations such as SF3B1, PTEN-only, or EGFR that may buffer PLK1 dependence.

features.basis: TP53 mutation present in almost all sensitive lines and absent in several resistant lines; p53 loss increases mitotic dependency
PLK1 is the primary drug target; higher expression increases dependence
KRAS mutations enriched in sensitive lung/pancreas/colorectal lines, may drive mitotic/RTK stress
SMARCA4 loss in several sensitive lines may impair chromatin-based DNA repair and increase PLK1 dependence
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with TP53 mutation in sensitive lines, further deregulating cell cycle
STK11 mutation in sensitive NSCLC lines may impair metabolic/checkpoint responses
SF3B1 mutations appear in multiple resistant lines and may alter splicing to reduce mitotic dependency
PTEN mutation without TP53 mutation in resistant lines may activate PI3K/AKT survival signaling
EGFR-mutant resistant glioma line suggests RTK-driven survival buffering PLK1 inhibition
BRAF mutations in resistant melanoma/endometrial lines may activate MAPK survival
ARID1A mutations in several resistant lines may alter chromatin state and reduce drug sensitivity
PLK3 is a secondary target; higher expression may compensate for PLK1 inhibition
